findings.title: Mutable database principal can bypass the empty-data guard and delete production data
findings.observation: Rollback derives the production Compose project from immutable attempt authority, but reloads databaseUser and databaseName from current process configuration. AttemptRuntimeBinding omits that principal. cleanupOwnedProject queries the supplied database and uses a zero result to authorize deletion of the target project's frozen container, network and volume identities.
findings.trigger: Persist a fresh failed attempt whose bound production database contains application rows, then recover FAILED/ROLLING_BACK with POSTGRES_DB changed to another existing empty database in the same PostgreSQL container.
findings.impact: Recovery proves emptiness against the decoy database, removes the production volume containing the real application data, and publishes terminal ROLLED_BACK. This violates the no-data-loss boundary.

evidence.description: An exact-head FakeDocker probe modeled one row in the originally deployed database and an empty decoy selected at recovery. Only the decoy was queried; the promise resolved ROLLED_BACK and container/network/volume counts all reached zero.

The host reloads config().postgresUser/postgresDb, the durable runtime binding contains runtime and previousEnvironment but not the current production principal, and cleanup deletes the frozen set after querying only the supplied database.
The mandatory fresh-context reviewer independently reproduced the same destructive false ROLLED_BACK with actualDatabaseRows=1, queriedDatabases=[decoy_empty_db], and zero remaining resources.
Automatic deletion requires proof that the production application database is empty, and destructive cleanup must not rely on ambient environment.

findings.remediation: Durably bind the non-secret production database user and name before the first mutation (for example in attempt runtime/lifecycle authority), derive every recovery cleanup query from that binding, and reject current-config drift before application callbacks, database reads or Docker mutation.
findings.verification: Add a controller/host crash-restart regression with data in the bound database and an existing empty current-config database. Require deterministic principal-mismatch rejection, no application callback, no decoy query, no Docker deletion, preserved resources/data, and no terminal success.

findings.title: The documented manual rollback entrypoint bypasses cleanup and terminal authority
findings.observation: The production-documented deploy:lp05:rollback command invokes rollbackApplication directly and maps application PASS or NOT_APPLICABLE to ROLLED_BACK. It never executes or resolves rollback cleanup, never verifies TerminalRollbackEvidenceV1, and returns early on the resulting terminal attempt.
findings.trigger: Run the documented manual command for a fresh persisted FAILED or ROLLING_BACK attempt while production or restore lifecycle resources remain, or after rollback-cleanup.json was persisted but the process crashed before terminalization.
findings.impact: A fresh install can be permanently journaled ROLLED_BACK with owned resources still present. Aggregate-crash recovery can repeat application rollback instead of reusing the immutable aggregate, contradicting idempotent recovery authority.

evidence.description: rollback-cli derives terminal state solely from the seven-field application result, unlike controller recovery through ActiveDeploymentOperations, cleanupReference and resolved terminal evidence.
The runbook exposes this command as the idempotent manual recovery entrypoint for exact persisted FAILED/ROLLING_BACK attempts.

The fresh-context independent review confirmed that application NOT_APPLICABLE writes ROLLED_BACK while resources remain and subsequent invocation returns early; existing aggregate authority is not consulted.

findings.remediation: Route the manual CLI through the same persisted runtime binding, executeRollbackWithCleanup, cleanup aggregate reconciliation and TerminalRollbackEvidence resolution used by controller recovery, or refuse terminal success unless exact-attempt terminal cleanup authority already verifies.
findings.verification: Add CLI-level fresh-install FAILED and ROLLING_BACK tests with live lifecycle resources plus an aggregate-persisted crash replay. Require exact cleanup/terminal evidence, one application invocation, no repeated deletion, and no ROLLED_BACK without resolved aggregate PASS.
